limitations: The full trial and collector use a phase-derived bounded deadline. Its original result is retained, including any failed delivery or environment gate.

The simultaneous scheduling gaps support an environment contribution but do not identify the host process, hypervisor operation or root cause; they do not retrospectively change earlier failed verdicts.
Baseline packet rows quantify loss for this trial only; they do not establish the cause of the previous sustained-loss failures.
Header captures, clock probes and the bounded host process CPU observation are diagnostic instrumentation, not a release performance repetition.
UTC is used only for bounded event correlation; clock probe gaps use monotonic elapsed time.
The host CPU observation has one-second granularity and itself consumes CPU; process coincidence does not prove causation. No unrelated application was stopped for this run.

hostTop.scope: Diagnostic scheduling attribution; top itself adds host observation work.

hostCPUObservation.processScope: one unrelated host application renderer; application-specific details retained only in private diagnostic logs
hostCPUObservation.causality: A simultaneous CPU burst is observed; an approved comparison with the unrelated application closed is still needed to establish its contribution.

findings: The complete instrumented relay run passes all 56 original acceptance assertions. Three minutes of baseline decode at a median 30 fps without a freeze; recovery reaches its target after 13.122 seconds and sustains it after 26.173 seconds.

Of 185086 primary RTP packets during baseline, five are absent between VM egress and ingress (0.00270145%). None are missing on either container/VM boundary. All 37017 observed FEC packets reach every capture point. All four captures report zero kernel drops.

A 0.219-second constrained-phase freeze coincides with an unrelated host application renderer consuming 5.457 cores. Concurrent independent timers report gaps of 67.619 ms on macOS and 96.652 ms in Linux; the browser timer is delayed by 160.4 ms. Wall-clock steps stay below 1 ms in that window.

This observed scheduling interruption is retained. Its size remains within this fixed-format runner's existing gates; the format runner has a different recovery-phase gate, which still rejects the prior 0.208-second event. No historical failed verdict is changed.
The previous sustained roughly 15-percent TURN loss is not reproduced here. Its underlying cause remains unassigned, and this instrumented diagnostic does not replace a repeated release matrix.
